Definition: probably the same as the base of G5530; to loan:--lend.
BiblicalUsage: Chrao means to lend, and it stands once, in the parable of the friend at midnight: a man knocks on his neighbour’s door and says, Friend, lend me three loaves. The Greek spells it chrēson, and the text behind the King James lemmatizes it as kíchrēmi, the older form of the same verb for lending.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the one place this word stands is a parable about asking: a neighbour who will not be put off, and a God who gives to those who ask.
